key_insight: OMOP can capture most demographics and medical-history variables in multi-site stroke rehabilitation research data, but it misses many detailed rehabilitation assessment subscales and items.
clinical_relevance: Better interoperability could make rehabilitation research data easier to combine for AI/ML and precision rehab studies, but current CDM coverage is incomplete for complex functional measures.
method: Mapped 46 demographics/medical history variables and 95 rehabilitation assessment variables from the ENIGMA-SR stroke recovery database to OMOP standard concepts.
Two independent raters evaluated whether each data element could be represented in OMOP and which specific concepts to use; disagreements were reconciled.
Coverage was summarized for overall inclusion and for granular subscale/item-level elements of complex assessments.
evidence_signal: Inter-rater agreement was good to very good for OMOP inclusion and concept mapping overall (Gwet’s AC 0.79–0.89), with final reconciled mapping reaching 100% agreement; OMOP covered 84.8% of demographics/medical-history elements but only 58.9% of rehabilitation assessments.
watch_item: Findings come from one harmonized stroke-recovery repository, so OMOP coverage may be even weaker for other rehabilitation domains, especially detailed subscales and item-level outcomes.
paper_title: Exploring the Application of the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model to Multi-site Stroke Rehabilitation Research Data
